sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Learned counsel for the appellant instead of pressing I.A.No.22768/2025, which is second application under Section 389(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code/430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant, prays that this appeal be heard finally.
2. Accordingly, I.A.No.22768/2025 is dismissed as not pressed and with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this appeal is heard finally.

3. This Criminal Appeal under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./415(2) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 15.04.2024, passed by II Addl. Sessions NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 2 CRA-7592-2024 Judge,
Multai, District Betul, in S.T.No.12/2023, whereby, the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under :-
 Conviction Sentence  I  Section Act Imprisonment Fine Sanju Vadiva vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83489650/

 376(2)(n) & IPC  376(3)
4.
Shri Irfan Khan, learned counsel for the appellant submits that this is a case where learned trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidence in totality.
It was guided by considerations other than the legal appreciation of evidence on record.

5. It is pointed out that Victim had made a complaint as contained in Ex.P/1 to the Station House Officer, Police Station Saikheda, District Betul that she is aged about 14 years, resident of Village under Police Station Saikheda and working as a labourer.

About 8-9 months back, she had gone for grazing of her animals when at about 06:00 P.M., appellant-Sanju Vaidiva came to her and asked her that he wishes to talk to her and in the name of such conversation had taken her forcefully to the bushes near Bajrang temple and violated her privacy.

Thereafter, on the pretext of life 5-6 times he violated the privacy of Victim, as a result of which, Victim became pregnant for seven months and,
thereafter, she reached the police station to lodge a report.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 3 CRA-7592-2024 6.

Shri Irfan Khan, learned counsel for the appellant submits that same is the tone and tenor of 'Dehati Nalishi' Ex.P/2 recorded on the basis of the written complaint Ex.P/1, showing time of incident from 01.10.2022 to 31.10.2022 and the 'Dehati Nalishi' was recorded on 19.05.2023 at about 17:30 P.M.
7.

It is pointed out that Victim was subjected to medical examination as is evident from MLC report Ex.P/8 by PW/2 and, thereafter, MLC of the appellant Ex.P/17 proved by Dr. Gokul Patidar (PW/6).
8.

This report is proved by Ravikant Dehariya (PW/12).

2 9.

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that when there is no allegation of gang rape and there are specific allegations made by the Victim that appellant was violator of her privacy, then in such a case despite recording a finding in para 45 of the impugned judgment that DNA report is negative and it does not prove NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 4 CRA-7592-2024 that appellant is the violator of the privacy and father of the new born child, yet learned trial Court has mentioned that only on those basis can the statement of the Victim is said to be contradicted ?

10. Thus, it is prayed by learned counsel for the appellant that it is a case of intellectual dishonesty in the hands of the learned trial Court by not appreciating the evidence in the correct perspective and passing an order of conviction by hook or crook which needs to be condemned because the impugned judgment is contrary to the evidence on record and, therefore, prayer is made to set aside the impugned judgment of conviction and acquit the appellant.
11.
Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent-State, submits that Victim at the time of the incident was a minor.
Her date of birth is mentioned as 15.09.2009 in Ex.P/14 proved by Sunita Uikey (PW/3).
Thus, it is not a case of consent.

It is also submitted that there is specific allegation on the present appellant that he had violated privacy of Victim and, therefore, the DNA report will not be of much significance, but after having said, he fairly admits that the conviction is based on incorrect appreciation of evidence.

12. Victim (PW/1), in cross-examination, admitted that appellant Sanju Vadiva is not of her village,
but is a resident of Village Khapa.
She admits that she does not know name of the father of the appellant, but appellant belongs to the same community and is related to her.
She admits that she lost her mother during her childhood and she lost her father when she was in 5th NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 5 CRA-7592-2024 Class.
She is residing with her brother and sister-in-law.

If it is not mentioned in Ex.P/1 as to how many brothers and sisters are there,
then she cannot give the reason for such omission.
She admits that she is 13 years of age.
If this fact is not mentioned in Ex.P/1 or in the case diary statement Ex.D/1, then she cannot give reason for such omission.
13. Victim (PW/1), in para 6 of her deposition, admits that she is stating on an estimation that her age is 13 years.
In para 7 of her deposition, she admits that date on which she had gone with her oxen for grazing is not remember by her.
In para 8, she admits that when accused had violated her privacy, she had not informed this fact to her family members.
She admits that she cannot give the date, month and day when the incident took place.
She admits that accused had given her a mobile phone, but if this fact is not mentioned in her case diary statement Ex.D/1, then she cannot give reason for such omission.
In para 9 of her deposition, she admited that accompanying with her friends, she used to visit appellant Sanju Vadiva.
If this fact is not mentioned in her case diary statement Ex.D/1, then she cannot give reason for such omission.
14. PW/2, is sister-in-law of the Victim.
She admits that age of the Victim is 14 years, but she does not remember her date of birth.
She admits that parents of the Victim are no more.
She further admits that Victim studied upto 6th Class in a Government School at her village and at present she was not studying.

Thereafter, this witness stated that two months prior to the date of her deposition Sanju Vadiva vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83489650/
3 i.e. somewhere in May 2023, Victim claimed of pain on her stomach, and then on enquiry, it was revealed that she was pregnant.

sentences.text: She narrated that appellant Sanju Vadiva violated her privacy.

Thereafter, they NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 6 CRA-7592-2024 had gone to the police station who had taken them along with Asha Karyakarta to Government hospital at Betul where with the consent of this witness, medical examination was conducted.

This witness was thereafter declared hostile and leading questions were put to her.
15.
Sunita Uikey (PW/3) Primary School Teacher, states that she is working as Headmaster in the Government Primary School Chhitapati w.e.f. 12.10.2010.
On 20.05.2023, she had received a requisition from Police Station Saikheda, to submit documents in regard to date of birth of the Victim.
According to her, seizure memo is Ex.P/11, which contains her signatures from 'A' to 'A' part and the certificate given by her is Ex.P/12.
She states that she had brought original admission register on which at Serial No.507, name of the Victim is mentioned with her date of birth as 15.05.2009.
In cross-examination, this witness admits that on Ex.P/13, entries are not made by her inher own handwriting.

She states that Victim was admitted in her school in the year 2009, but she started taking instructions w.e.f. 2014.
16.

Sunita Uikey (PW/3), also admitted in her cross-examination that in Ex.P/35 entries which have been made from Serial No.494 to 514 reflects date of birth of different children starting from 2004,
2005 & 2006.

This witness also admits that the name of the parents for the student whose name is mentioned at 506 and that of the Victim is identical and caste is also identical.
17.

Thus, it is evident that when parents of Victim were not available and the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 7 CRA-7592-2024 sister-in-law PW/2 admits that she does not know the date of birth of the Victim corroborated with the evidence of PW/1 Victim who states that she is giving her age to be 13 years on the basis of estimation.
When these facts are read with the evidence of Sunita Uikey (PW/3), School Teacher, it is evident that prosecution has failed to prove the age of Victim to be minor at the time of the incident.

This fact has been admitted in para 19 of the impugned judgment by the learned trial Court that the concerned page of the original register Ex.P/35 is in a torn condition regarding entry No.507.
18.

We have perused the original register Ex.P/35, which is in a torn condition, but on going through the entry at Serial No.507 as mentioned by PW/3, it is evident that the entry of date of birth is torn and on that page which shows admissions to have been made in 2011-2012, date of birth of most of the candidates is of the year 2005-06.
A an entry in regard to the Victim is completely torn on the second page.
Thus, certificate Ex.P/12 showing her date of birth to be 15.05.2009, is incorrect.

19. We have no hesitation to confirm our finding that date of birth mentioned as 15.05.2009, is incorrect, inasmuch as, admission could not have been taken by the Victim at the age of 2 years in Class-I, because Sunita Uikey (PW/3), admitted that though Victim was admitted in the year 2011,
but she started taking instructions in 2014.

Sunita Uikey (PW/3) also admitted that her father had come to get the Victim admitted on 20.06.2013 as is made out from Ex.P/13, then original register which has been produced, appears to be a fabricated document.

sentences.text: Sunita Uikey (PW/3), also admitted that at the time of admission, no document was produced in regard to her date of birth.

Thus, it is evident that not only Ex.P/35 is a concocted document which does not pertain to the Victim, but also Ex.P/13-C, clearly reveals overwriting in the date of birth of the Victim and, therefore, Ex.P/13-C saying that Victim had taken admission on 20.6.2011 in Class-I at 02 years of age, is not made out especially when in Govt. school admission in Class-I cannot be given admission below the age of 05 years.
Therefore, prosecution has failed to prove the age of the victim so to attract the provisions of POCSO Act.
21. Dr. O.P. Yadav (PW/5), Radiologist, stated that Victim was brought to him for sonography.
He had conducted sonography, report of which is Ex.P/16.
He had found that Victim was pregnant for 30 weeks 5 days and the date of possible delivery was 24.07.2023.
22. Dr. Rupal Shrivastava (PW/9), is the lady doctor, who had examined the Victim and had advised investigation as to the pregnancy.
She categorically admitted that she had not advised for X-ray for age determination as Victim was pregnant.
23. Dr. Kalpana Singh (PW/10), had obtained blood sample of 18 day old infant.
She had also taken blood samples of the Victim along with her child and preserved them.
Identification form of the Victim is Ex.P/20 which contains a photograph.
She had taken not only her blood sample, but also blood sample of the new born vide Ex.P/21, sealed them, preserved them and handed over to police for examination.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 9 CRA-7592-2024 24.
Rajwanti (PW/11), is the witness in front of whom blood samples of Victim and her infant child were drawn.
25. Ravikant Dehariya (PW/12), is the Inspector who had carried out inspection.

In para 21, this witness categorically stated that if DNA report would have been received by him prior to filing of the charge sheet, then also he would have filed the charge sheet, but would have looked for other accused persons.
26. In the present case, firstly, prosecution has failed to prove age of the Victim.
Onus was on the prosecution to have proved beyond reasonable doubt that Victim was minor at the time of the incident.

Since prosecution has failed to prove the age and there are several interpolations and manipulations in the school record, tacitly admitted by Sunita Uikey (PW/3), School Teacher, we are of the opinion that firstly prosecution has failed to prove the age of the Victim to be minor and,
therefore, provisions of POCSO Act cannot be applied in a mechanical manner.

Our view is fortified with the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court in Aabad Harshad Ponda Vs. Union of India and others, Writ Petition (Crl.) No.382 of 2024, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that provisions of POCSO Act is increasingly being misused in cases arising out of marital discord and consensual relationship between adolescents.

The Court stressed the need to spread legal awareness Sanju Vadiva vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83489650/
5 among boys and men about the penal consequences of such offences.

sentences.text:
26. This PIL was filed firstly, seeking a direction to promote public NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55581 10 CRA-7592-2024 sensitisation regarding laws governing sexual offences and the POCSO Act.

Secondly, when DNA report is negative and it clearly says that the new born is not a biological son of the appellant Sanju Vadiva, then taking these facts into consideration,
conviction merely on the statements of the Victim, which are not corroborated through any other evidence, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

Impugned judgment having been passed on conjectures and surmises without proper appreciation of material evidence and without taking into consideration a fact that in para 9 Victim has admitted that she used to visit appellant Sanju Vadiva along with her friends, prima facie the element of force and coercion gets nullified on its own.

When the oral testimony is not supported with documentary evidence and the expert medical evidence,
then conviction cannot be sustained.
27. In the result, appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment of conviction against the appellant is hereby set aside.
Appellant be released forthwith if not required in any other case.
Case property be disposed of in terms of the orders of the learned trial Court.
Record of the learned trial Court be sent back in a sealed cover.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (AVANINDRA KUM  JUDGE JUDGE  A.Praj.
